speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the duration of these episodes and whether there is any loss of bladder control or tongue biting during them. Have you witnessed these events happening to you or someone else?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the boy had any recent fever, head injury, or been taking any new medications? REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram). REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side. MRI_Brain: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Patient
text: c and confused afterwards. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous suggestion of Multiple Sclerosis is highly unlikely given the patient's age and the specific description of a "muddy taste" preceding the events; MS is rare in 7-year-olds and typically does not present this way. Has the boy experienced any seizures involving loss of consciousness or jerking movements in the past, and does he have a family history of epilepsy? REQUEST TEST: Genetic_Panel. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_with_epilepsy_protocol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Seizures (likely evolving into Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy given the hand gestures). The normal EEG and MRI rule out structural causes or typical absence seizures, suggesting the "hand gestures" may indicate a focal onset or evolving syndrome. Please ensure follow-up with a neurologist for video-EEG monitoring.
